name: Filename Cleaner
description: Strip characters that break filenames on Windows, Mac or cloud uploads, and see exactly what would be replaced.
body:
Result

Your cleaned filename will appear here.
howto: Type or paste the filename (with extension) into the input.
Pick the platform you are uploading to — this controls which characters are illegal.
Choose the replacement character (a hyphen by default).
Review which characters were replaced in the detail list, then copy the cleaned name.
features: Platform-specific rules for Windows, Mac/Linux, cloud uploads and strict-all
Live detail of every character replaced
Protects against reserved names like CON, PRN, NUL

faq.a: Windows forbids < > : " / \ | ? * and control characters, plus reserved device names like CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9 and LPT1-9. The Windows preset handles all of these.

faq.q: What is different on Mac and Linux?
faq.a: Mac and Linux only forbid the forward slash (/) and null bytes. The tool still replaces other awkward characters for safety but applies the stricter Windows rules only on the Windows preset.
Cloud drives often reject certain characters and reserve names too. The cloud preset keeps it safe for Drive and Dropbox while staying friendly.

faq.q: Does this rename my actual files?
faq.a: No. It produces the cleaned name for you to copy. To rename many files at once, use the Batch File Renamer.
